title: Sergio Ramos Consoled a Tearful Messi After Spain Won the World Cup Final
excerpt: Former El Clásico rivals turned PSG teammates shared an emotional embrace on the pitch after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in extra time at the 2026 World Cup final.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Sergio Ramos consoled a tearful Lionel Messi after Spain's World Cup victory over Argentina.
  • Spain won the final 1-0 in extra time, securing their second World Cup title.
  • Messi scored eight goals in the tournament, finishing second for the Golden Boot.
  • Ramos, a World Cup winner in 2010, carried the trophy during the post-match ceremony.
  • This match likely marked Messi's final World Cup appearance at age 39.

  • Sergio Ramos made a beeline for Lionel Messi after the final whistle, hugging and consoling the 39-year-old who was in tears on the pitch at New York New Jersey Stadium.
  • Ramos, who won the 2010 World Cup with Spain, had earlier carried the trophy onto the pitch for the post-match ceremony.
  • Messi scored eight goals across the tournament but could not prevent Argentina's 1-0 extra-time loss to Spain, likely his last World Cup appearance.

Moments after Spain clinched their second World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina on Sunday, cameras captured one of the tournament's most poignant images: Sergio Ramos walking straight to a devastated Lionel Messi, wrapping him in a long embrace near the center circle.

The gesture carried decades of history. Ramos and Messi spent the better part of 15 years as fierce adversaries across the El Clásico divide — Ramos at Real Madrid, Messi at Barcelona — before fate threw them together at Paris Saint-Germain in 2021. What had been one of football's most intense rivalries became an unlikely friendship.

"I am no longer surprised by Messi. At Barca he was used to deciding games like he did today. I'm glad he's on my team now. My relationship with Messi is excellent. There is great respect among the players."

— Sergio Ramos, during their time together at PSG

A Painful Night for Argentina

The final, played before a capacity crowd of over 80,000 at New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford, was a tense, tactical affair. Neither side managed to break the deadlock through 90 minutes. Argentina's task grew harder when center-back Cristian Romero received a second yellow card in the third minute of stoppage time, leaving the Albiceleste a man down heading into extra time.

Spain capitalized in the 106th minute when Ferran Torres converted off an assist from Nico Williams, sealing the victory. Argentina threw everything forward in the final minutes — two corners, two free kicks, a throw-in in the dying seconds — but could not equalize.

Messi, playing in his third World Cup final at the age of 39, was left crestfallen. He had scored eight goals across Argentina's tournament run, finishing second to France's Kylian Mbappé (10 goals) for the Golden Boot. But the final was one match where his influence could not tip the balance. Spain's 68 percent possession and 20 total shots to Argentina's two told the story of a dominant performance.

Ramos: From Trophy Bearer to Comforter

Ramos, now 40, had been given the honor of carrying the FIFA World Cup trophy onto the pitch for the post-match ceremony — a nod to his role in Spain's 2010 triumph in South Africa. But before the celebrations kicked off, the veteran defender sought out his former teammate and longtime rival, according to reporting by Get Spanish Football News.

The image resonated far beyond the stadium. Ramos made "a beeline for Messi on the pitch, hugging and consoling the defeated attacker," OneFootball reported. It was a rare display of cross-national solidarity at the sport's biggest occasion — two players whose careers defined an era choosing empathy over triumph.

Messi Breaks His Silence

On Monday, Messi addressed the loss in an emotional Instagram post.

"The pain is immense, and it will take time for this wound to heal. But I also hold on to all the good. This group reached two consecutive World Cup finals."

— Lionel Messi, via Instagram

He thanked Argentina's fans and congratulated Spain on their victory. "Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and every message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and be together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentinian," he wrote, according to People magazine.

Spain's 18-year-old wunderkind Lamine Yamal also sought out Messi after the final whistle, sharing a handshake and embrace with the man who had famously held him as a baby during a charity photoshoot. "I did the photo when he was a baby and to face him in the World Cup, it's crazy," Messi had said before the final, according to USA Today.

The End of an Era

With Messi turning 43 before the 2030 World Cup, this was almost certainly his farewell to the tournament that shaped his legacy. His record stands at 21 goals and 12 assists across six World Cup campaigns, spanning from 2006 to 2026 — a run that included the 2022 triumph over France in Qatar.

Argentina reached the final for the third time in the last four World Cups, a feat that underscores the golden generation Messi captained. For Spain, the victory means back-to-back major tournament titles after Euro 2024, led by Yamal, Williams, and a midfield marshaled by captain Rodri.

The Ramos-Messi moment will endure as the defining image of a final that closed one chapter and opened another — two legends who once defined a rivalry, united in what football demands after the final whistle: respect.
